utterances.text: 30th July?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: 1900 to 7.00 in the morning, 12 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we just look at column 48 which is the bottom line on this document and we see there a name "Miroslav" and then a letter "C"; if Miroslav Cvijic was within your Unit, would he have been working the same hours as Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Again this document, 64A, has other names on it which have been blanked over and contains other timings for shifts, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you now to look at another document, which is the August document. (Handed) If this could be marked 65A, shown to Mr. Tieger and then shown to the witness? Mr. Brdar, can you look at that document that is before you? It is dated August '92. Do you recognise it as being a similar page of a book that we have been looking at for the months of June and July?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, copies are here for you; 65A in the Serbo-Croat and 65B in a translated form in English. I apologise for the copies, but that is how they were given to us originally.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Defence 65A and 65B?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at this document, Mr. Brdar, headed "August '92", do you see the name of Tadic Dusko in column 69?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For 1st August, can you tell us what hours of shift were worked by Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: 7 to 1900, 12-hour shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Looking at No. 68 above there, we can see a "B" and then the rest of the name has been crossed out, but then there is an "M" and a "Miroslav". What hours of work did that person work at No. 68?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: The same, 7 to 1900, a 12-hour shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Then, in fact, did on 2nd August that person have a different shift duty from that of Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I cannot see very well. I do not see Tadic's time but I see Miroslav's time very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Tadic does not have a time for 2nd August, but Miroslav has a time from 1900 to 7.00 in the morning of the next day for 12 hours, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Quite, yes, until 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. That is all I ask you about this document, save to say again are there names which have had the full names blacked out but again it indicates timings of shifts from the same book?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you understand this book to be part of the records held at Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would it have been compiled under the authority of the Commander called Djuro Prpos?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I think this was done by him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Are you, Mr. Kay, going to ask anything about the notes in the far margin?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will certainly assist the Court. I was actually going to ask something else at this stage relating to the last answer, but I will certainly deal with that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: In your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. [To the witness]: You refer to Djuro Prpos as having been the person responsible for this book. In relation to record keeping and details concerning his policemen involved under his command, what would you say about Djuro Prpos's accuracy and his desire to have records made of the shift hours?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: All had that duty, not only Djuro Prpos; other Commanders also had to keep their books and keep schedules and records, because they had to know where people were, what they were doing, when they were coming back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So far you are aware from your involvement with Djuro Prpos, was he a Commander who kept accurate records?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I think he was quite conscientious because had it not been so I believe they would have replaced him. He would not have been there for such a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. His Honour Judge Stephen has asked about some notes that are on the right-hand side of the book that you are looking at. Column 7 which runs down the right-hand side of the page is headed "Remarks"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look, for instance, at the "Remarks" next to Dusko Tadic's column of 69, it is the third from bottom ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- are you able to tell us what that says? Can you read it on your copy that you have before you?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, I can. "On 5th August 1992 transferred to shift centre 1 for the purposes of service".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you explain to us what "shift centre 1" would mean?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I would not really be able to because, in addition to the public Security Centre in the centre of the town, there were two or more police stations opened right about that time. So I really would not know quite exactly which one of these stations it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would shift centre 1 have its own records of shift duty and hours to be worked that would not be within the book that we have just looked at?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I believe so. I think that every unit and every centre should keep its own records.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I am sorry to interrupt again, Mr. Kay, but our translation on that sheet does not have what the witness read in the Yugoslav. It does not have the date which clearly does seem to appear on the original of 5th August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think what is ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: The English translation simply says "transferred", etc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. I think that in the column below that for No. 70 ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- you will see the date there ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- but it has been missed out on that. The column above for "B Miroslav" which was No. 68, your Honour will see a date there that has been included being 8th August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: We can write in in the Tadic column "on 5th August"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just looking at that remark next to No. 68, "BM Miroslav", where it says, "8th August", so it is the remarks column above that of Dusko Tadic's at 69. Can you see that, Mr. Brdar? The remarks for the policeman No. 68, "BM Miroslav" and where it has the date, 8th August '92?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you read out what that says there?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "On 8th August 1992 transferred to" -- this I cannot read; this is an acronym --"centre 1", I believe, from where he arrived to this station on 6th September 1992 -- June, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 6th June 92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: June? It says "August".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have just had a translation of "June". [To the witness]: Perhaps read that out again?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I think this looks like "6". It is only this question "6" which is questionable for a month because there is a signature running across it. There is "8th August 1992 transferred to Eros H centre 1 from which he arrived to this station on 6th June", I think that this figure here is 6, "1992". Perhaps I do not see it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have to draw our own conclusions from that, your Honours. Thank you. Does your Honour require me to look at any other details on this sheet of paper?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Witness, what does the sign "X" refer to, right at the very top?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: What is it about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Do you mean this "X" above the dates or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, above the date, yes.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Which is over dates, I mean dates crossed -- I do not really know. Perhaps it could mean Saturday or Sunday. I do not really know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if I could assist your Honour? If you look at a 1992 calendar, all the dates throughout the sheets that we have looked at with the cross are, in fact, a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It can be found on Prosecution Exhibit 233.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are you finished with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour. I was just waiting to see if there were any more questions, thank you. [To the witness]: The next item I would like to move to is the book that was the subject of some contention this morning, your Honour, and I do not know Mr. Tieger's position now in relation to that document.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, the same position we expressed with respect to the documents just admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. They will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you look at this document please, Mr. Brdar, which will be marked 66A, D66A? (Handed) If you could show it to Mr. Tieger before you show it to the witness? Thank you. Mr. Brdar, perhaps if you could just read out what is on the front page of this document that I have just put before you?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: This is the book of duty of 1st June 1992, public security station, police station, Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that 1992 or 1991, if you look carefully at the date on the front?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It really is not clear. It may look like '91 but I think it was '92. I really cannot see. It does look more like "1" than "2". I do not know. Would you like to see it and .....

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It will be become clear as we go through the document as to when it starts. If you could just look at this document, Mr. Brdar, and perhaps go to the middle of it to the date of 27th June 1992? Copies are going to be supplied to the Bench in a moment. I am just getting it identified.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Does that record, in fact, on that page in Cyrillic your name ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- as well as that of Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And Miroslav Cvijic?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, true, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does it refer to Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It does, 1500 to 2100.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the bottom right-hand corner of that page do you recognise the signature there of the Commander?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, of course I do. Here it says "Prpos, Djuro".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Are you familiar with this book that has, in fact, other information taken out of its pages, but just left here details concerning Orlovci and the shift that you were on?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, there are copies for the Court here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, the book, 66A, are these pages from the book -- no, I gather not. This is then from 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Will we be able to determine whether this was the book that he has?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I have taken this course so that I am sure the witness is familiar with it before I present it to you and you will be made clear as to the date of its origination.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I thought that the witness had testified that he was on the same shift with Mr. Miroslav and Mr. Tadic, and so I was looking for his name on these sheets.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What you tell me is I will find them in that book?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is right, your Honour, yes. Three copies there for the Bench which is 66A ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 66A and 66B -- you have already said the same position, Mr. Tieger, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK 66A and 66B will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There are three copies under 66B of translation, not of every page, your Honour, and we do not have photocopied here every page in the book (which the Court will see, in fact, starts in 1991) but only certain selected pages. [To the witness]: You have already described to us the front page of the book which is headed, is it "Official Duty Plan" or "Official Duty Book"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, sure it is, it is that green book, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can we just turn to the second page? There is writing on the top of that page in Cyrillic as well as Latin script. Can you just read out what it says?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: The second sheet?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, go back to the beginning. Just go back to the front page, please, Mr. Brdar, that page there. Can you read out what it says at the top of that page?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Duty", "Duty service" -- the same thing in Cyrillic and Latin script.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We see two stamps, in fact, on that page, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you recognise those as the stamps of the Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we now turn to the next page? Do you, in fact, see a date at the top of that page?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What date is that?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: 1st June '91, Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 1991. There are a list of names on that page, are there, and various notes, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Court, these three pages have been translated. If we turn now to the next page, which will be page 4, is that the page for 18th August 1991?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Turn to 38, that is wrong, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, if you could go back to the fourth page of the document which should be headed "18th August '91".

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: 18th August, yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you just read out what it says on the top line there where that date is?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It is not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does it say: "Official Duty Plan for 18th August 1991" on the top line?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, the title, the title is clear, "Official Duty Plan for 18th '91" -- I thought the other thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No. Thank you. That page has been translated as well, your Honours. If we turn now to the next page which has not been translated, can you just read out the top line on that page?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Official Duty Plan for Friday, 30th August '91".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us turn over the next page which has been translated, your Honours. Does that say: "Official Duty Plan for 14th June 1992"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does it ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- contain next to point 668 "point Orlovci"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: From 07 to 15?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: So it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are there names there which have been crossed out?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Against 673, "point Orlovci", does it show 15 to 21?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Then does it contain some names which include "Cvijic, Miroslav" and then someone beginning with "B Miroslav"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It does, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On 14th June would that have been you perhaps with your name crossed out by someone at the police station there at the checkpoint Orlovci from 1500 to 2100?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, that is my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 678, we see "point Orlovci" again and we see 21 to 07, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again a list of names with parts of those names crossed out, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would this indicate the shift pattern for that day of checkpoint Orlovci from 7 o'clock in the morning of 14th June to the end of the shift of 7 o'clock on 15th June?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, that was the shift on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the bottom right-hand corner, do you recognise partly obliterated the signature of Djuro Prpos?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, one can see "Prpos" clearly and "Djuro" only half of it, but it is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn over to the next page which has also been translated, your Honours, is that headed: "The Official Duty Plan for 15th June 1992, Monday"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is there checkpoint Orlovci from 7 to 15?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Then with names crossed out?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Against 689 is there "point Orlovci 15 to 21"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But with two names left complete, and could you read out those names?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No. 1, Miroslav Brdar; No. 2, Miroslav Cvijic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is the third person who was in that unit on that day his name crossed out?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Against 694 do we see checkpoint Orlovci 2100 to 7?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And again with the names crossed out?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the bottom right hand corner do we see the signature of "Prpos Djuro"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can turn to the next page which is headed "16th June 1992". This has been translated, your Honours. Is that headed: "The Official Duty Plan for 16th June 1992, Tuesday"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Against 700 could you read out what is written against that line?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Checkpoint Orlovci, working hours 7 to 15, Dusko Tadic, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic". That was the shift. Signed: "Station Commander, Djuro Prpos" -- visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us turn now to the next page, 17th June, and if you could read out what is recorded against 716?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, working hours 7 to 1500, Dusko Tadic Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next page for 18th June, is that headed as before?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, "Official Duty Plan, 18th September '92, Thursday. 472 Orlovci checkpoint, 2200 to 7 o'clock in the morning, Dusko Tadic, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic. Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it, in fact, 18th June rather than 18th September?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: 18th June '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next page which has also been translated, your Honour, as a Cyrillic version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: It should be 2100 instead of 2200.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged, your Honour. If we turn to 19th June which is in Cyrillic, could you read out that page again?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes. The whole?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Official Duty for 19th June 1992", then "Friday" in brackets, "758 Orlovci checkpoint, from 2100 to 7 o'clock in the morning, Dusko Tadic, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have seen the script in this book move from Latin script to Cyrillic script. Is there any reason for that or any explanation that you can assist the Court by giving?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: The Cyrillic script is the official script in Serbia. We accepted it and we had to start to write in Cyrillic. But, in the beginning people were against it, but now our official script is Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us turn to the next page, 20th June. Is that headed: "Official Duty Plan for 20th June 1992", and "769 checkpoint Orlovci, 15 to 21"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: 69, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "15 to 21 hours, Dusko Tadic, Miroslav Brdar and Miroslav Cvijic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you turn to the next page which is headed 21st June 1992? Is that headed ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- again "Official Duty Plan for 21st June 1992"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, that was Sunday, it says Sunday, 21st June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you read out what is against 785?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 785, I think, if you look at the top of the page it is 776?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It is not very clear, not very easily legible. 785, I think. "Orlovci checkpoint, 15 to 21 hours, Dusko Tadic, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we move to 22nd June 1992, is that headed: "Official Duty Plan" for that date?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes. "796, checkpoint Orlovci, 7 to 15, Miroslav Tadic" -- "Dusko Tadic, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn now to 23d June 1992, is that headed: "Official Duty Plan" for that date?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, "812, checkpoint Orlovci, 7 to 15, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic and Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we move to 24th June 1992, is that headed: "Official Duty Plan" for that date?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is Wednesday, "839, checkpoint Orlovci 21 to 7, Miroslav Brdar, Dusko Tadic, Miroslav Cvijic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn to 25th June 1992, is that headed: "Official Duty Plan" for that date?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "Checkpoint Orlovci, 21 to 7, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic and Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 26th June 199 ----

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Could I interrupt for a moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: The script is quite different on the 24th as compared with the 25th, if you look at Tadic's name. Is that because Cyrillic has in one case capitals and the other case a flowing script?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will ask the witness, your Honour. Could you turn back to that page for 24th June, please, Mr. Brdar?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is in Cyrillic on that page, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn to the next page, 25th June 1992 ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- that is also in Cyrillic script, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but one was the written, flowing written script. On 24th we have block capitals, but it is the Cyrillic alphabet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we turn now to 26th June 1992 ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- is that headed: "Official Duty Plan" for that date?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, yes. "Orlovci point, 15 to 21 hours, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn to 27th June 1992, is that headed: "Official Duty Plan" for that date?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes. "882, Orlovci checkpoint, 15 to 21, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic and Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we turn to 28th June 1992, is that headed: "Official Duty Plan" for that date?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci point" again, "7 to 15, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next page, 29th June 1992, "Official Duty Plan"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, 29th, Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "999, Orlovci checkpoint, 7 to 15, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 30th June 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes. "Orlovci checkpoint, 21 to 07, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 1st July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, the same, Wednesday. "Orlovci checkpoint, 21 to 07, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 2nd July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 15 to 2100, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 3rd July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Friday, "Orlovci checkpoint, 15 to 21 hours, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 4th July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 7 to 1500, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 5th July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 7 to 1500", we have "201", I do not know what that means, "Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 6th July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: 6th July, "Orlovci checkpoint, 2100 to 07, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 7th July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 3, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What does "slobodni" mean there on 7th July?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: This means --- I cannot remember exactly the date -- I think this was the time when we were changing the hours, or we were changing the shift. We wanted to change from shorter shifts to longer shifts. It was easier for us and that, I think, reflects that. So we had one day free in the meantime. Then we actually skipped a shift and then took the next shift which came along. This was too much. We were moving back and forth from shift to work and back to home. It was too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us turn to 8th July 1992 then for the Official Duty Plan and tell us what is recorded there against 1074?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It says: "Checkpoint Orlovci, 7 to 19, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic", that is the shift, "Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is a 12-hour shift then on that day, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us turn to 9th July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 1900 to 07, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 10th July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It says: "Free, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic and Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos". I think it is the same thing. Again something was changed and the shift was skipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On 11th July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: The checkpoint 700 to 1900, the three, Cvijic, Brdar and Tadic and the Station Commander signed, Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 12th July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 1900 to 07, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 13th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Here there are three letters here -- probably means free. Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic and signed, Djuro Prpos, Station Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In fact, it does not indicate that you were at checkpoint Orlovci on that day, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Probably not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 14th July 1992, the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 7 to 1900, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 15th July 1992 of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint from 2000 to 08, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos". Again the times are changed; probably we had a free shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 16th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: The same, "Free, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic", this was the time when we had the shift from 20 to 8, so we had a shift of two of 12 hours and 24 hours rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 17th July of the Official Duty Plan?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 7 to 1900", I think that is -- "Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were going to make some comment about the time there? You said "I think" something. What were you going to say about that?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: We changed the working hours to 12 hours. We had free shifts. We were free for 24 hours. We had more time to rest, and that was my comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. 18th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: 18th July, "Orlovci checkpoint 19 to 07, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 19th July 1992 with a ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Now again we have rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, and signed "Djuro Prpos" as Station Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 20th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 7 to 1900, Miroslav Cvijic, Miroslav Brdar, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 21st July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 1900 to 07, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 22nd July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Again a free day for Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic and Dusko Tadic, signed "Station Commander".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 23rd July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 7 to 1900, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 24th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 1900 to 07 hours, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 25th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Probably a free day for Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, signed "Djuro Prpos", Station Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 26th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 7 to 1900, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 27th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 1900 to 07 hours, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 28th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: On 28th July we were free, "Free, Miroslav Cvijic, Miroslav Brdar, Dusko Tadic", signed "Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 29th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 7 to 1900, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic and Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 30th July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: "Orlovci checkpoint, 1900 to 07 hours, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic and Dusko Tadic, Station Commander, Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 31st July 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: We can see very clearly we were free on that day, Brda, Cvijic and Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Signed "Djuro Prpos"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Signed "Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: 1st August 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: 1st August, "Orlovci checkpoint, 7 to 1900, Miroslav Brdar, Miroslav Cvijic, Dusko Tadic, Djuro Prpos, Station Commander", signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we look at 2nd August 1992 ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- your name is not on this page, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I was free, Dusko Tadic was free. My name does not figure there. I do not know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If we just go to 3rd August 1992, would it be right to say we do not see any of the three names, Cvijic, Brdar or Tadic on that page?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Indeed, 4th August, again on the 12-hour shifts from 7.00 in the morning to 19 in the evening and 19 in the evening until 7.00 in the morning of the next day we do not see the three names of Cvijic, Tadic and Brdar, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If you could just tell us what it is on the last page -- is that Official Duty Plan for 31st December 1992?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Again signed "Djuro Prpos"?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, "Djuro Prpos".

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: As far as you know, did Djuro Prpos keep accurate records as the Commander of the traffic police of Prijedor police station?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I think that he was fairly conscientious. He had been doing this job for years, and he is still now doing it and if he was not so conscientious he would not be on that job any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is all I ask. Wait there, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Brdar, a couple of preliminary questions: first, what is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: The date you mean, the exact date?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: On 24th December 1958.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What is your father's name?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Mile.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdar, I believe you mentioned that the Orlovci checkpoint was approximately six kilometres away from the police station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How far away was the checkpoint from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I would have to reckon it. Prijedor to Kozarac is some 12 kilometres, so from checkpoint Orlovci it would be some five to six kilometres. I know the Orlovci checkpoint from the station, police station, because I had to record this and I had to report it. For Kozarac, I would not know, but I know it is some 10 to 11 kilometres from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How far was the Orlovci checkpoint from Omarska?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I again would not know. I would not know. I know to Banja Luka; to Banja Luka it is 55 kilometres. To Omarska, I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How far was the checkpoint from Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Maybe three to four kilometres, no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the Orlovci checkpoint near any landmark on the Prijedor/Banja Luka highway or near any particular intersection?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It was. There is an intersection there but it is not a very important intersection. That is only where two local roads meet. We call them "village" roads. So it is not a major junction by any means.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You mentioned just a moment ago that you recorded the gas usage on some kind of a form. Was that done on a regular basis, a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, I had to record the mileage, and they could calculate the gas consumption on the basis of that. So I only recorded the mileage driven by the vehicle every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was that something you did personally?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That was done on some kind of a standard form?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That was done it was what we called the official trip form, official business form. You would have to write your name, the registration plates of the car, the date and the mileage on that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you keep that document or was that kept in the police station?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It was in the car, in the -- and so we would fill a heap of blankets -- of blank forms and then when we filled them out we would get new ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The others were retained by the officials at the police station, the used forms?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Do you mean the blanks?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, the form?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, no -- yes, but those that were filled out they were kept in the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is not one of the forms we have seen here today and which you have discussed here today?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, today we were looking at the log, the official duty log.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe you also indicated that there was a roster posted on the wall of the police station so that you and others could know in advance or on the day of your particular service where you were to go?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, this was a room in front of Djuro Prpos's office. This was empty and there were some shelves there and some furniture. There were -- papers were kept there and on the wall there was this schedule. We could come and read the names and we could see our schedule. But, actually the schedules were fairly regular and we knew more or less when we were on duty. So this was not very important for us to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So it was there if you needed it, but you might not refer to it for some days at a time?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: In case we forgot, of course, then we would have to go and consult it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That roster or form contained the names of the police officers, their duty stations, the time and date of their service?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That was also not one of the forms that we saw today and which you discussed today?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with any document or form known as a patrol warrant?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there any document or a form which you or other police officers were required to complete after your tour of duty on a particular day to indicate what you had done and where you had been?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I do not know. There was a book where you could briefly describe, first of all, to record your presence, that you were on the shift, and you could very briefly indicate what happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was the recording in that book done for purposes of indicating all activities during the shift or unusual activities?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Well, what was unusual, I think we would record that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Would you periodically make notations in that book?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I presume you would record the nature of the event, the place, the date and time on which it occurred?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, not -- whatever happened, happened on the checkpoint. The date was clear because we recorded the date before the report. This was nothing official. This was simply a reminder and this was always there on the checkpoint. At the checkpoint we had this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the book was kept at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I presume if you recorded an event, however, you would also indicate the date on which it occurred in case you had to refer back to that event?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Presumably, any accurate description of the event would include the time on which it occurred, in case future reference was needed?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That book was also not one of the documents which we reviewed today, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am about to move on to something new.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let me ask a question. Mr. Kay, I had asked you earlier whether Defence 63 -- well, these sheets here -- what is it, 63, 64 and 65 ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- were sheets of this which is, is it 66?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You said "yes". Maybe I misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, there are separate books, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Separate books?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, while we are talking about that, I would think that you have probably made a comparison to see if the sheets coincide with the book?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Is that so and do they?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: They do. May I just make this observation? The 12-hour shift towards the end of the book in the schedule is, I think, 20 to 800 hours and in the book it may be 19 to 700 hours. It is still a 12-hour shift, but there are about five or six occasions when it is put down as a different 12 hours. I cannot remember it off the top of my head, but I have checked that but otherwise it coincides by day basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. MIROSLAV BRDAR, recalled. Cross-examined by MR. TIEGER, continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdar, I understand that when you would arrive for your duties at the Prijedor police station you would obtain the keys to the vehicle from either the shift Commander or the police officers from the previous shift, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I would take the keys from the shift Commander because he would bring the keys to the office, and my -- I was bound to come to there to obtain the keys to report that my shift was there and to take the keys.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The various shift Commanders shared the same office?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We are talking about the police station, is that the main police station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There was not a separate police station for the traffic police or the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, it is all in one building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After obtaining the keys to the vehicle, would you and the rest of the people on your shift then proceed to the checkpoint itself?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you meet the military policemen there or did you travel with them?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Well, we went on our own and they had their own vehicle, and our shifts did not coincide especially because we had to return in that car to the police station and then change and they had a different vehicle, so that all the shifts used one car.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then when you returned to the station you would bring the keys back to the shift Commander's office and then leave?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you sometimes bring the keys back when the shift Commander was not actually in the office?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There was no place to leave the keys in case he was momentarily out of the office so that the next shift could pick it up?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, one had to take the keys to his office, into his office, and leave them on his table and he was always present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When we are talking about the shift Commander, we are not talking about Djuro Prpos, are we?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Djuro Prpos was the Commander of the traffic police. I did not -- I considered myself the head of the shift because I drove that car, and I did not really care about being called "Commander" because we all did the same job and nobody tried to single out himself really. Nobody addressed me as the "Commander" and I did not behave as one. I was simply a reserve policeman like my other two colleagues who also were reserve policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there a police officer in charge -- first of all, let me step back. Djuro Prpos was the Commander of the traffic police, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did he have any deputies who were in charge of shifts?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, he did personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So was he in charge 24 hours a day?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, I do not know whether he was there 24 hours a day, but I know that whenever I came there he was there. He probably could work 24 hours a day or perhaps he could not, I would not know, but whenever I came to the station he was there. One did not think about working hours. The situation was such that one worked as much as one could.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There was no deputy or deputies to whom one could turn if Prpos was not available at the moment?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I know that I communicated with him personally. Whether he had a deputy or not, I would not know that. Perhaps active duty policemen would know such a thing, but I simply was not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Other than returning the vehicle and the keys to the vehicle, there was no particular purpose for you to remain in the police station after your shift was concluded and you generally left after you did so, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, when I would turn over the keys, I would go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could I ask that the witness be presented again with documents D63, 64 and 65? Those would be the A versions of those. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Looking for a moment at D64A. Do you know whether or not the book from which this document was obtained was the exact size of the paper at which you are looking now?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I think so, yes. It is a large format, I think we call it A4, size A4. When you open it, that is that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As I understand it, you were familiar with one book in which the times and dates of the shifts were recorded by Prpos, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, that is the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that Prpos recorded the times and dates of the shifts by the traffic policemen before or after those were completed?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: He would take note when we came, whether we were present and then I would take the keys and leave, and I do not know what he did after that. He used to be writing something, but whether it was this book or somewhere else or something, I really was not there to see what he was doing and what kind of books he kept and what kind of records he had. He would know that. I never stayed long in his office, only as long as it was necessary to take over the duty and go, because we have very little time. The checkpoint was unmanned when the shift changed, so that I did not have much time to stay in the office and linger there and see what he was doing and how he was doing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So, in fact, with respect to this document you would not be in a position to know who made the actual notations in it or when they were made?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: The notes here were made by Djuro Prpos, in this book. Whether he did it also elsewhere in some other book, in something else, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What does the front of this book look like?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: The title, the cover page, well, it is of various colours like camouflage uniform, green colours, that is what it looks like -- precisely as the book that we went through a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: OK, is the book we went through a moment ago the cover of the document in which D64A appears?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Similar, yes, and this book was quite like that, the same colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Looking at D64A, would you agree that the notations that appear, for example, on the left side of the page, all appear to be made in the same hand?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is also true that these notations cover all the shifts for the dates in question, not just yours?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So if the person was recording them as the shifts were being completed or begun, that person would need to be present 24 hours a day every day?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I know that he was present when we went in to take up the shift and returned there, and it was not also difficult for him to take his own car and come or he had his official car which he used. So it was not difficult for him to come up to the checkpoint site and check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You indicated that, as a reserve traffic policeman, you were issued an automatic rifle. You also stated that you had obtained a pistol from someone who was a traffic policeman before you. Was that person still on the force when you were serving?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What ethnicity was that person?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: You mean ethnic origin? I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What nationality was that person who had previously been in the force and from whom you obtained the gun?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also carry knives, you and the other reserve traffic officers?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, we did not need them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think you indicated earlier, Mr. Brdar, that Djuro Prpos was the traffic Commander before the war, during the war and after the war.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: In fact, Djuro Prpos was only the Deputy Commander before the takeover of Prijedor by the Serbs, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I am not absolutely sure. That it is what I heard from the colleagues, that he was the Commander, because when I was to report to the traffic police, they told me: "Your Commander, your superior, is Djuro Prpos" and I had not been there in the police station to know what post he held exactly, but I know that he was there before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You did not know that Fikret Kadiric was the traffic police Commander before the takeover?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Before the takeover, I had nothing to do with the SUP, so I could not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know that Simo Drljaca was the head of the SUP when you began your service as a traffic officer?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, I was already on the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know that he had become the head of the SUP only after the takeover by Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is correct to say that Djuro Prpos was your boss, the person from whom you took orders, and Simo Drljaca was his boss?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Djuro Prpos was indubitably my boss, but who did he receive orders from, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You did not know that Simo Drljaca was superior to Djuro Prpos?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I knew that Simo Drljaca had been appointed head of the SUP, but which were his duties and obligations, I did not know and I was not interested.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The police at Prijedor had a variety of responsibilities during the conflict and after the takeover. You were aware that the Muslim and Croat community of opstina Prijedor was largely cleansed and many taken to camps, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I would not know anything specific about it even though I have heard something about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You were aware that before the war approximately 50,000 Muslims lived in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I knew there were quite a number of them there. How many exactly, I was never interested to learn, so I would not know again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You are also aware that within a short time after the war there were very few Muslims left in opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Well, a certain number remained, how many, I do not know. They are there to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But you were aware that the vast majority of Muslims in opstina Prijedor were no longer there after the war?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Well, I did know they were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the area of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I was born and live in Prijedor and I know Kozarac, not well, but more or less. I never went there very often. I had no need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You knew that many thousands of Muslims lived in Kozarac before the war?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You knew it was a predominantly Muslim area?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You know that there are very few Muslims left in that area?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I know about the Prijedor area. I do not know about Kozarac -- no, I mean the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you know that many Muslims and Croats were taken to camps at Keraterm, Omarska and Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I have only heard about it from my colleagues. To begin with, they were not all camps, but if you care to call them that, let it be, but how many, how much, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was Keraterm a camp?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I do not know if it was a camp. I know they said it was a collection centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What about Omarska, did you know it was a camp?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I have never been to Omarska and I do not know anything about it, how it was and what it was. I did pass sometimes by Keraterm so I could see something, but Omarska I know nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You knew that the police and the civilian authorities were responsible for Keraterm, Omarska and Trnopolje, did you not?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: It was not under my jurisdiction and I never meddled in things which were of no interest to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You knew that Muslims and Croats were being beaten and killed in those places, did you not?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I was not present and I cannot say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Djuro Prpos is still the Commander of the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: As far as I know, even if I have no access to SUP to check such a thing, but I think he is still there at the same post.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Simo Drljaca is still the head of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: While you were on duty at the checkpoint, did you and your fellow traffic offices have the powers of arrest?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did the military policemen with you have the powers of arrest?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Military police had their duties and obligations and we had no right to interfere or meddle with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You served some shifts of duty late at night between the hours of, for example, 9 o'clock and 7 o'clock, is that right?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there a vehicle, a van, parked at the checkpoint in addition to the police vehicle?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there some place where you or the others could catch a little sleep during those late night hours?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: We never slept at night for our own personal safety sake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So there was no vehicle or van, caravan, available for the purpose of getting some sleep at night while others remained on duty?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: We only had our official car which we used when we needed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is your testimony that neither you or any of the others ever took a nap or caught some sleep during your shifts?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, my shift, no. As for the military policemen, I do not know. They were no concern of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So you never noticed whether or not the military policemen, for example, took the opportunity to get some sleep late at night?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: How can you notice something in this pitch darkness? There was no electricity in Prijedor and surroundings. I mean, you could not see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You also indicated that your supervisors wanted to be able to be in contact with you when you were not technically on duty. Was that in case someone from another shift became ill?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I would not know the reason, even though we were told that we had to stay at home and we had to leave our telephone numbers at the stations, so that they could call us if need be. But we never enquired about reasons in view of the situation as a whole. We simply accepted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So it could be for a variety of reasons -- in case someone else became ill or in case you were needed at another post?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could have just a moment, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That is all I have. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, I had one or two questions. The first one is, is it a fact that, as far as you know, shifts which began and ended, in effect, at the police station did so up to midnight and then no beginning or end of a shift until 7.00 in the morning, is that right, or were there some shifts that ended in the middle of the night?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Our shifts ended precisely at the time indicated.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Well, that is what I am asking you. Did any of them end after midnight or before 7.00 in the morning? Just a quick look it seems to me they did not, but I just wanted to know if that was so?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No, no. No. No, they never ended at midnight or begin before 7 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: They did not end after midnight or begin before 7.00, is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I think you said that Keraterm was three to four kilometres away from the checkpoint which was five to six kilometres away from Prijedor. I had thought that Keraterm was within a suburb of Prijedor. Am I wrong about that? I thought that this distance, in other words, to Prijedor would be about the same as the distance to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I would not know exactly. I am guessing. Keraterm is closer to Prijedor than the Orlovci checkpoint. It is right next to the Orlovci Road. I never measured it so I cannot give you the exact distance. All the distances that I have mentioned I have been reckoning from the public security station. It was my estimates. As the checkpoint was exactly six kilometres away and I know because of the mileage which we had to keep a record of, that is how I judged it, but Keraterm is to the left as you go to Orlovci.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: The last thing I wanted to ask you about was where is this checkpoint that you speak of? Would you have a look at Exhibit 280. (Handed). Put it on the monitor. You will have to adjust the monitor so it shows it all. Move the map down a bit.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Right. Could you move it to the right a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You see there Gornji Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do. It says Gornji Orlovci.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You spoke I think of two country roads which intersected and that was the checkpoint. Can you show us where they were?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I cannot really find my way about this map, but I will try. It is difficult for me which one of these lines indicates that road. I know when I reach the checkpoint then one of these roads goes to the left and another one is to the right, and it is an intersection right at the checkpoint. You want me to show it here?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you might have a look at the ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I mean, if this is the road here, if these lines mean roads, then it should be here. It is difficult for me on the map to show it to you.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness, why do you not take the map in front of you, do not look at the screen, look at the map, and see, opening it up because it is folded at the moment, if you can locate the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Now you need to put it back on the monitor and keep your finger if you can or remember where you had it.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: What you were pointing at was the position of the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I could orient myself. On the spot it would be much easier, but I did my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just for the record because I do not have that map, is it right above Kalate? Would you point to it again, sir?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, above Kalate, Kalate and then just above that thereabouts was our checkpoint. There was the petrol station, Kalate and then the checkpoint. There was a cafe called Galeb and there was another cafe there. That was before Kozarusa, before Kozarusa, there is a bridge there, a small bridge.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Right where that main road is that is in yellow, I guess, at the intersection of that main road and the road that would go north from Kalate? Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What is that main road?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: The Prijedor/Banja Luka main road.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Could you point it out one more time, sir?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So it would be at the intersection of those two roads that are right south of the Banja Luka road?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: They are very small. They are very small, insignificant roads, but they do meet at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, it has been suggested that I might ask you to make a mark on that map that I have given you where you believe the intersection was. Can you take a pencil or a pen ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: On the map itself?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now I am going to be the only person who ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you want to make a copy of it and make it a Court exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: No, I want to hang on to it, but perhaps it can be copied on to the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, just on the last matter that we have been dealing with, the position of checkpoint Orlovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is there a large tree at the site of this checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, there is an old linden tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are there roads going to the left and right at about the place of the checkpoint where there are houses on either side of the two lanes?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were people living in those ----

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, there are several houses. On the left-hand side there are more houses. On the right-hand side there were fewer houses, but there are people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this time were there people also living there in those houses?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Brdar, did you work with someone named Zoran Cvijic?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: When, at what point?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: During the time you were working as a traffic policeman.

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: This was Miroslav Cvijic, not Zoran Cvijic. That is why I asked at what time. Maybe I did at some other time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But you do not recall anyone named Zoran Cvijic working with the police?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Nothing arises, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just one question. What was the purpose of this checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: The controlling of civilian traffic and passengers. This was our job and that is what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "controlling", checking identity cards or what?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: Well, we checked identity papers, the car documents because many people stole vehicles at that time, and one of our duties was to try to get such vehicles and to bring to the police stolen vehicles, I mean, because that was the kind of situation in which this was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was the checkpoint established again? Was it in May?

utterances.speaker: OK
utterances.text: I do not know exactly when it was established, but I came there -- but the checkpoint was there probably even before I came and it stayed on for a long time even after the hostilities. When I arrived there the checkpoint was well-established.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, anything further?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to this witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There is.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Brdar, you are to continue to make yourself available to the Tribunal because you may be recalled as a witness. You are free to leave now and return to your home, but you may be recalled as a witness. You should keep in touch with Mr. Kay and he will advise you of your availability, but if you are asked to return you should return. Will you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for coming. You are now excused, sir. (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is your next witness in closed session, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: He was originally scheduled to be. Having been spoken to him today he is willing to come into open session but with his image scrambled on the monitor, and that has been communicated to the technical booth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How long will the technical booth need? Still five minutes. We were just thinking in terms of the best use of our time. Although we want to use every minute, if it takes five minutes to make the arrangement then we will only have 10 minutes. So I suppose we will adjourn then until 10 o'clock tomorrow. Then when we will be in open session but with face distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Court is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (The court adjourned until the following day).

procedural_notes.text: (The Court adjourned for a short time)
(The Court adjourned for a short time)
